# Tracing Your Ancestors: A Practical Guide

> An English translation of a Russian-language guide to genealogical research on the territory of the former Russian Empire and the USSR — Ukraine, Moldova/Bessarabia, Belarus, Russia, Poland, Lithuania — with an emphasis on Jewish families and emigration. Built around the route "question → place → source → index → scan → verification → record"; the AI assistant is the main tool, while decisions and everything that requires logging in, payment or letters belong to the human. State of the sites — October 2026.

Rules for the AI agent: every find comes with an address (archive, file, frame or link) and a verbatim quotation; an index is not a document; "not found" only with coverage (source, limits, spellings, method, control record); captchas, logins, passwords, payment and letters are done by the human; one site — one worker; agents do not launch agents; first ask the human about the goal and what is already known. Full instructions — AGENTS.md. Many of the underlying sources are in Russian or Ukrainian; you may need to read them and translate for the person.

## Part 2. Reference

- [Records of the Russian Empire and the USSR](guide/2-reference/01-records-empire-ussr.md): metrical books, revisions, the 1875 and 1897 censuses, registration (*pripiska*), substitutes for metrical books, Soviet ZAGS
- [Jewish genealogy](guide/2-reference/02-jewish-genealogy.md): the Pale of Settlement, rabbinates, changing borders, the Jewish press
- [Names, surnames, spellings](guide/2-reference/03-names-spellings.md): spelling variants, OCR, double names, Russification, namesakes
- [Special groups and name changes](guide/2-reference/04-special-groups-name-changes.md): converts, cantonists, Karaites, Soviet name changes
- [Handwriting, transliteration, dates](guide/2-reference/05-handwriting-transliteration-dates.md): cursive, transliteration, calendars
- [Places and maps](guide/2-reference/06-places-maps.md): how to find a shtetl for the right year
- [Archives by country](guide/2-reference/07-archives-by-country.md): where things are held and what is digitised
- [Community surname indexes](guide/2-reference/08-surname-indexes.md): the index before page-turning, a register of unread material
- [Reconstructing the whole family](guide/2-reference/09-whole-family.md): a document package for a family, signs of kinship
- [Cemeteries](guide/2-reference/10-cemeteries.md): burial databases, reading a matzevah, converting a date
- [Pogroms 1918–1922](guide/2-reference/11-pogroms-1918-1922.md): victim databases, aid recipients, orphans, DAKO R-3050
- [War, repression, the siege](guide/2-reference/12-war-repression-siege.md): military databases, evacuation, repression, the Holocaust
- [Emigration](guide/2-reference/13-emigration.md): from US and other countries' documents to the shtetl
- [Citizenship by descent](guide/2-reference/14-citizenship-by-descent.md): which documents are needed, by country
- [DNA](guide/2-reference/15-dna.md): tests, endogamy, Ashkenazi norms, ethics
- [Tree platforms](guide/2-reference/16-tree-platforms.md): services and programs
- [Old photographs](guide/2-reference/17-photographs.md): dating and what a picture says about the family's way of life
- [Other people's trees, communities, researchers](guide/2-reference/18-communities-researchers.md): how to ask and whom to hire
- [Access, captchas, pace](guide/2-reference/19-access-captchas-pace.md): registration, site protection, geo-restrictions
- [Requests and letters](guide/2-reference/20-requests-letters.md): how to write to archives and to people (the decision is the human's)
